title: Music director for Plantation Days; lodging the band in his house
summary: He takes the second company of Plantation Days though he had never been in a pit, and later warns musicians not to house their sidemen.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So that's what happened. And then, when I come out of Baron's -- here's another chance in my life, and I'm showing about the chances that they had in those days, it was a show, it was the second company of "Plantation Days". Was being organized. And they were looking for a music director. Well, now, I had never been in a pit in my life.
They said, if you only needed nerve and carfare, you could go around the world. So I took this job on.
Well, were you on the street then, or were you at the Nest?
So this was a touring company.
And I'll show you one little joke about this. I bought this house, I bought a house on 129th Street. I had all my boys in the house, so I was taking their salaries and all like that.

Well, now, when we got out of a job, I paid $275, I had to pay a month when I first got this house. Before I bought this house in the next block. They all got out of work. When we got out of work, the boys all come to me and said, "Well, Sam,

you know we're working with you and you ain't working. So we can't pay no rent." Well, I had an awful time. I remembered that in the future. Anybody that ever hears this interview, don't ever take the men that you're working with on the job, in where you live. Because when you're out of work, they're out of work.
And all of this weight falls on you, because you can't put them out.
Well, anyhow, that's what happened, anyhow, so they all got other job, see? They eventually got jobs.
